findings.claim: The plan has `kmctl plugin install` stop writing the SessionStart hook and okf's MCP server. But install also supports `--scope user` for Claude Code. At that scope kmctl currently writes the hook into $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json and adds okf-bundle with `claude mcp add-json --scope user` (plugin.py install_mcp, settings_path). The plan, its success criterion and all three spikes cover only a project install. If `apm install -g` does not deliver the split package's hook and server, user-scope installs lose both. The migration step (remove kmctl's own SessionStart group and a stale okf-bundle) is also only described for project files, not for ~/.claude.json and the user settings.json. APM 0.33.0's source suggests it works: the claude target has user_supported=True, and the Claude MCP adapter writes $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json. But nothing has run it. The plan should say what happens at user scope, backed by a spike. Spike question: with ~/.apm/apm.yml holding {git, path: apm, ref} for the split package, does `apm install -g --target claude` write the SessionStart hook into $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json (recorded in its apm-hooks.json), write okf-bundle into the user .claude.json, and resolve ./claude without error? And over a user install today's kmctl wrote, does it leave two hooks, or skip a stale okf-bundle?

User scope was not covered. The plan now states that `apm install -g` writes the hook and okf-bundle into the Claude config folder, that the same migration applies to settings.json and .claude.json there, and that `apm uninstall -g` leaves okf-bundle behind. Spike 5 backs each claim.

doctor's claude.files and antigravity.files no longer cover kmctl's rules in a real install. APM records the rules under the sub-packages' own lock entries (name kmctl-claude, virtual_path apm/claude; kmctl-antigravity, apm/antigravity), but _deployed reads only kmctl_package(lock), the name kmctl / virtual_path apm entry. With .claude/rules/okf-bundle.md and .agents/rules/okf-bundle.md deleted from a real consumer, doctor still printed ok for both files checks. test_antigravity_files_cover_kmctls_rules_again passes only because the fake lock in tests/test_doctor.py (_package) puts the rules under kmctl's entry, which real APM does not do.

drop_old_hook drops a whole SessionStart group if any of its hooks runs kmctl briefing and APM did not record the group, so a user's own hook in the same group is deleted too. A settings.json group of [echo mine, kmctl briefing] came out as {}. Older kmctl replaced its hook in place inside whatever group held it, so mixed groups do exist. This breaks r4's 'every other hook stays'. unhook() in the same file already keeps the other hooks (rest = ...). drop_old_hook should do the same for unrecorded groups, with a test for a mixed group.

r6's integration test does not check what fails_when names after apm uninstall. It lets .claude/settings.json, .agents/hooks.json and .agents/mcp_config.json stay without checking that okf-bundle and the Stop wrapper are gone from them (hook_present needs both hooks, so a leftover wrapper alone passes), and it never reads .mcp.json, which lies outside .claude/ and .agents/.

r1's command (-k split_package) does not run the assertion that the shared apm/.apm/ holds no instructions, or the check of the Claude rules' applyTo. Those live in test_package_holds_the_skills_and_the_agent and test_package_rules_apply_to_the_old_globs_with_the_old_bodies, which only r8 runs. Move them under the row's selector, or widen the selector.

Two places give the install steps in the wrong order. The plugin install/update help epilog and the overview's plugin install row both say kmctl removes the old hook and okf-bundle first, then runs apm uninstall on an old entry. install() runs remove_old_apm_entry first, as commands.md says. Also, doctor's claude.hook and claude.okf-mcp details still say 'the hook this kmctl writes' and 'not the one this kmctl writes', though APM writes both now.

entries.change: kmctl_files folds the kmctl-claude and kmctl-antigravity lock entries into kmctl's package, so doctor checks the rules; drop_old_hook removes only kmctl's hooks from an unrecorded group and keeps the user's.
The files checks read kmctl_files; claude.hook and claude.okf-mcp say kmctl's package ships or declares them.
The install help lists the old-entry uninstall before the removal of the old hook and okf-bundle, as the code runs them.
The plugin install row lists the steps in the code's order.
The sample claude.hook line matches doctor's new wording.

The fake lock lists the rules under kmctl-claude and kmctl-antigravity as real APM does; the real-install test checks that uninstall leaves no okf-bundle in either MCP file and no kmctl hook in .agents/hooks.json; expected messages updated.
A migrate test keeps the user's hook in a group shared with kmctl's old one.
A split_package test checks the shared .apm/ holds no instructions and the Claude rules keep their globs.

findings.claim: doctor's files checks missed the rules APM lists under the kmctl-claude and kmctl-antigravity lock entries
drop_old_hook removed a whole SessionStart group, including a user's own hook
r6 uninstall assertions did not check okf-bundle and the Stop wrapper were gone
r1's selector missed the no-instructions-in-shared-package and Claude-rule assertions
help and overview gave the migration order backwards; doctor details said kmctl writes the hook and MCP server

kmctl doctor --help still describes antigravity.hook as checking the plugin folder's hooks.json ("its hooks.json" after .agents/plugins/kmctl/) and okf-mcp as "as this kmctl declares it"; doctor now checks .agents/hooks.json and the package's declaration
